column1: # Dangling path references in committed Markdown that are legitimately unresolvable,
# and why. Read by `scripts/ci/check-doc-path-refs.py`.
# Format: <path>\t<category>\t<reason>   ("#" starts a comment)
# Categories, and what each one is claiming:
#   runtime-path     the product creates this at run time (in the user's home, or in the
#                    directory it was started in); it is not repository content;
#   recorded-absent  the citing sentence itself says the file is missing, was removed, or
#                    never existed in this repository;
#   historical       the citation was true when written and the tree has moved since; the
#                    sentence is a record, not a pointer;
#   other-root       the name is relative to a different root than the repository: the
#                    pager crate's docs/ tree, upstream's tree, or the reader's own project;
#   planned          the file is meant to be created later by the plan that names it;
#   quoted-text      the span is text *about* a path (a bare depth fragment, or a link whose
#                    depth is the subject of the sentence), not a pointer to open.
# Four things this list can never do, by construction of the guard:
#   * excuse a broken Markdown link. Only inline code mentions can be recorded here; a
#     link that resolves nowhere is a defect and is reported whatever this file says;
#   * keep working after the reference is fixed. An entry with no live dangling hit is
#     reported as stale and has to be deleted, so this cannot collect permanent waivers;
#   * carry an unnamed exemption: the category has to be one of the six above and the
#     reason has to be at least 20 characters;
#   * excuse the same path twice. A duplicate path fails outright.
# No entry may use a category loosely: the guard refuses an unknown category, a reason
# under 20 characters, and a duplicate path. `runtime-path` currently has no entry,
# because the guard's anchor rule already drops runtime trees structurally (their
# top-level directory owns no tracked content); it stays in the vocabulary for a runtime
# path that would be written under a top-level entry that does, such as `./.agents/`.
# --- Text about a path, rather than a pointer to one -------------------------------
